evidence: gpt-oss precomputes "allowed pairs"; deepseek uses "1,2,3 = colors" and rejects only when "color[nb] == c"
affordance_in_statement: The displayed characteristic matrix together with the requirement that its "determinant must be non-zero" makes det(C_{u,v}) = (s_u - s_v)^2, so every link simply requires unequal multipliers.
removal_suggestion: Replace the matrix coefficients with a genuinely nontrivial, orientation-aware pair constraint and revise the parenthetical claim that swapping u and v is equivalent; keep the examples' stated outputs valid under the revised constraint.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Reduces each matrix test to a precomputed compatibility relation, effectively graph coloring with three values.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The determinant-nonzero condition on the displayed matrix.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats every edge as a proper 3-coloring constraint and searches colors 1, 2, 3 in order.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The matrix condition simplifies to requiring neighboring oscillators to have different multipliers.

common_affordance: The determinant condition is exactly the proper-3-coloring constraint s_u != s_v.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Enumerates all multiplier assignments, causing exponential brute-force time and TLE at n = 40.
Miscomputes the determinant as (s_v-s_u-2)(s_v-s_u)(s_v-s_u+2), incorrectly forbidding additional unequal pairs.

recommended_edit: Change the characteristic matrix so its determinant is not a square of s_u-s_v—preferably making compatibility depend asymmetrically on the ordered pair—and remove or revise the claim that swapping u and v gives an equivalent condition.
regression_risk: gpt-oss-120b may still survive because its implementation precomputes the matrix-derived compatibility table rather than hard-coding only inequality.
